explanation: Mixture. Strongest on 'ton(s)' in 'proton(s)' (physics or MRI). It also fires on the word after comparative 'more' or 'long' ('more than/then/that/the', 'long enough'), on 'asymptotic', on 'radiotherapy', and on scattered word-piece completions (Starbuck, randomised, midpoints, immunostaining).

Fires mostly on middle word pieces of long technical or chemical names (hepar-in, cyclodextr-in, phencyclid-ine, hydrochlor-ide, hyaluron-idase, methic-illin, flaviv-irus). It also fires on unrelated tokens: code punctuation like '(),' or closing brackets, and 'to' in 'used to convert'.

Weak, diffuse unit. It fires on tokens inside technical identifiers and code: version or model numbers (STM32, sha384), dots in IP addresses like 127.0.0.1, file and include names. It also fires on odd word pieces of foreign or proper names. There is no clear single concept.

Fires on the function word right after a quantifier, comparative or modal construction, completing a fixed phrase: 'more/less than', 'may not be in', 'anything you', 'no files to', 'cannot be', 'any of these'. The context matters more than the token itself; isolated content words give little or no activation.

Fires on the last word piece of rare, multi-token proper names, especially foreign place names, people's names and Latin species names (Albertslund, Cakobau, Köpenick, geoffrensis, Peshekee). It is strongest on the closing piece of a non-English word. Ordinary English words do not trigger it.

Mixture of tech-boilerplate and climate tokens. In software boilerplate it fires on the version number in 'Apache License, Version 2.0', on 'governed' in license headers, and on protocol or config names (AWS4, tcphdr, SELinux). In climate text it fires on 'carbon' (dioxide) and 'emission'/'abatement'.

Fires on tokens inside names of institutions, organizations and places, especially after 'College of', 'Ministry of', 'Professor of' or 'Royal ...'. It also fires heavily on word pieces in German and other non-English European text (Landesvorsitz, Anschluss, Asuntos, segurança).

Fires inside long identifiers: digits in the middle of long ID numbers (DOI strings like ppat.100372, Hacker News item ids, comment ids) and pieces of code identifiers (Class, _class, $method). There are also some scattered prose tokens with no shared theme.

Fires on the opening of an argument or list right after a function or list header: '(' after 'function' or after 'aims are:' / 'hypotheses:', '(2)' list numbers, reducer arguments like 'action'. A few unrelated prose tokens also fire.

Mixture. It fires on 'appeals' and 'for' (appellant/appellee) in legal case headers, and on 'EDIT'/'modify' in 'DO NOT EDIT' / 'do not modify' auto-generated notices. It also fires on assorted tokens in news datelines, code identifiers and other prose.

Fires in emotional, spiritual or inspirational writing (song lyrics, reflections on meaning) on abstract nouns or determiners about feelings and transcendence: 'something (bigger)', 'peace', 'a feeling', 'a sense of', 'wonder', 'humanity'. The uplifting context is what matters; the same words in neutral political or technical text barely fire.

Mixture with no clear theme. It fires on 'Files' in 'Program Files', on '.' in reporter citations ('So.2d'), on 'ui'/'shinyUI' in R Shiny code, and on assorted technical nouns in prose ('in place of', 'ion propulsion', 'control').

Fires on a head noun that completes a common fixed phrase: 'truth' (the truth is, Truthout), 'art' (art director, the art of, works of art), 'battery life', 'access control', 'session management'. The token in a set phrase matters most.

Fires on 'to' in 'may refer to' / 'can be used to refer to' (disambiguation phrasing), and on 'Hindu'. It also fires on a scattered mix of other tokens (code identifiers like catcode and session_start, 'grabbed hold', 'chest radiograph').
